newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Sverdlovsk shifts Eurobond issue to Oct.
newsitem.headline: Russian Sverdlovsk shifts Eurobond issue to Oct.

text.p: Russia's Ural region of Sverdlovsk has shifted its Eurobond issue plans to October from August, a senior Inkombank official said on Wednesday.
Inkombank is the adviser on the issue.
"The issue will most likely be in September, or to be even more realistic, in October," Vice-President Rafael Nagapetyants told Reuters.
Sverdlovsk's Eurobond project provides for a total $300 million paper in several issues over several years in three to five year paper, he said.
He declined to mention the volume of the first issue, but previously regional authorities have said the initial volume would be $100 million.
WestMerchant Bank is lead manager of the project.
"It is long money and not at the interest rate offered to us by small creditors," Sverdlovsk deputy governor Galina Kovalyova told a news conference.
She said the region was now converting its accounts to international standards with the help of KPMG.
WestMerchant Bank Vice-President Gene Chayevsky said he expected healthy demand for the Sverdlovsk issue after St Petersburg's Eurobond success.
He said the fact that St Petersburg Eurobond was placed well right after the City of Moscow Eurobond launch and just ahead of Russia's issue testified to interest in Russian paper.
"There is a significant demand for Russian securities on the Western market," he said.

The City of Moscow placed a $500 million Eurobond in May at a spread of 315 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. St Petersburg launched its $300 million paper last week at 312.5 basis points. Russia is now holding a road-show for its third Eurobond.
Kovalyova said the region would use the proceeds from the paper for ecological and military conversion programmes.
